summary: Phase 14 (legacy migration + activation + redirects + wishlist display) tested end-to-end. Backend: test_phase14_migration 7/7, test_phase13_wishlist_alerts 3/3, new test_phase14_t1_extended 6/6 (all run with -n0). Importer CLI: the dry run wrote nothing (collection counts identical before and after in the app DB and the staging DB) and reported all 5 planted errors plus the duplicate_email and invalid_email items (exit code 1). The real import into test_database_qa14 had a clean verification block; a rerun created or updated nothing (idempotent). --target-db test_database was refused. The qa14 DB was dropped. Frontend: the login activate link, the generic request message, the error for a bad token and for mismatched passwords, and the full valid activation all work: /login?activated=1 shows the notice, sign-in reaches /account and /auth/me returns 200. Legacy redirect /product/qa-old -> /products/<slug> works, /product-tag/palm-oil -> /search?q=palm oil works, and an unknown path shows the 404 page. Wishlist at 1920 and 390: in-stock and out-of-stock items show the price, the out-of-stock item shows 'Out of stock', and the discounted item shows the price-drop badge. Admin guards hold: 403 mfa_required without MFA, 403 for customers, 422 for every wrong confirm text, 409 for a batch while unapproved, 422 for batch_size 0 or 201. Approval was never turned on and is still OFF. Found 1 security issue: activation re-enables suspended accounts.

critical.issue: A suspended (or deactivated) migrated account that holds a valid activation token can complete activation. The handler then sets status='active', which silently undoes an admin suspension. The find_one_and_update filter does not exclude INACTIVE statuses, and $set forces status 'active'. Reproduced in test_phase14_t1_extended::test_request_for_normal_or_suspended_account_issues_no_token: the response is 200 {status: activated} and the user's status changes from suspended to active. Realistic path: a bulk activation email goes out, then the admin suspends the user, and the old link still works.

minor.issue: A token shorter than 10 characters (e.g. /activate?token=bad) returns a raw Pydantic 422 message, 'String should have at least 10 characters', and the UI shows it as-is. Users will think the message is about their password. Return the generic invalid-link message instead (a 64-character bad token already gets the correct text).

The static legacy redirects (/about-us, /contact-us, /faqs, /privacy-policy, /become-a-vendor, /stores...) exist only as legacy_redirects docs that the importer writes. The app DB has 0 redirects, so /about-us shows a 404 today. Consider resolving STATIC_REDIRECTS in code, the way /product-tag/* is handled, so they work no matter which DB was imported.

Counts are taken with estimated_document_count after mongodump finishes. On a live DB, collections that are written during the dump (audit_logs, rate_limits, sessions, analytics_events) can differ, so restore_verify may report a false FAIL in production. Consider excluding volatile collections from the strict check or allowing a tolerance for them.

ui_bugs.issue: /activate?token=bad shows the raw text 'String should have at least 10 characters' instead of the invalid-link message

issues: The Wishlist card still says 'Saved items will appear here once wishlists launch with product discovery (Phase 05)'. The copy is stale: wishlists already exist.
The 'Out of stock' pill (text-av-muted on bg-av-line) has fairly low contrast; consider darker text.
The 'checked' state is never reset when the pathname changes. Going from one 404 path to another does not show the checking placeholder (minor, functional anyway).

action_items: complete_activation: add {status: {$nin: INACTIVE}} to the update filter (or check _needs_activation(doc) before consuming the token) and stop forcing status='active'. Add a regression test.
Map short or malformed activation tokens to the generic 400 'invalid link' message (drop min_length on token or catch it).
Optionally resolve STATIC_REDIRECTS in /redirects/resolve so they do not depend on the import.
Update the stale Wishlist card copy on the Account overview.
critical_code_review_comments: migration.py activation_batch: when _needs_activation(doc) is false, the claim timestamp is left set. This is harmless but leaves stale claims behind.
importer.py: the refuse-live guard compares only target_db == settings.db_name. That is OK, but --allow-live-db bypasses it with no second confirmation.
restore_verify.sh: with set -e, the restore_check DB is not dropped if mongorestore fails partway.

success_rate.frontend: 95% (all requested flows pass; 1 low-priority message issue)

seed_data_creation: qa14_ui_seed.py created a TEST customer, a TEST vendor with 3 products, wishlists, a migrated user with an activation token, and the /product/qa-old redirect. All of it was removed with 'python -m tests.qa14_ui_seed cleanup'. The app DB is back to users=1, products=0, legacy_redirects=0, wishlists=0. test_database_qa14 was dropped. migration.activation.approved is still false.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run the Phase 14 tests with -n0; pytest.ini adds xdist. Activation endpoints have a 10/hour per-IP rate limit. test_phase14_t1_extended clears rate_limits keys matching ^activate in setup_function. The live DB has no products, so use tests/qa14_ui_seed.py (writes /tmp/qa14_seed.json with customer cookies, product slugs and a raw activation token) for UI checks, then run its cleanup. The staging DB test_database_migration_staging was created by the main agent and left in place. After the fix, the suspended-account case in test_phase14_t1_extended should assert a 400 and status 'suspended'. Right now it only prints the result.
rca of the issue: complete_activation (auth.py ~L214) consumes the token, then calls find_one_and_update with the filter {_id, migration.activation_required: True, password_hash: None} and $set status='active'. It never checks the current status. Repro: insert a migrated user with status 'suspended' and an activate_account token, then POST /auth/activation/complete. The response is 200 and the status becomes 'active'. Fix: add 'status': {'$nin': list(INACTIVE)} to the filter and remove 'status': 'active' from $set.
